title: First trip to Europe in 1962 with Basie and the George Wein tour
summary: Edison went to Europe with Basie for three months and stayed a year, and describes the Wein package with Hawkins, Miles Davis and others.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You were saying -- you said earlier that after you left Basie, you went back and played with him from time to time.
Oh, yes.
When would that have been?

Let's see, I took a trip to Europe with Basie in 1960, '62. 1962, I went with Basie. I went for three months and stayed a year, you know? And that's when Jaws* was with the band. We did some dates over there with Tony Bennett. Let's see, was that '62? I think it was, because my first trip to Europe was with the George Wein Newport thing. That was Coleman Hawkins, Howard McGhee, Thad Jones, J.J. Johnson, Sonny Stitt, myself, Miles Davis.
Oh, that was kind of --
Jo Jones, Sir Charles Thompson Jimmy Wood . Oh, he had a big aggregation.
This was George Wein?
Yeah, yeah.
Where'd you play?
*Eddie "Lockjaw" Davis.
Well, the groups broke up, went in different directions, you know.
Oh.
Like we would -- Coleman and I, we teamed together, with Jo Jones, Jimmy Woodé and Sir Charles. We went all through Spain, --
Yeah, that makes sense.
Yeah. We went all through Spain and then we went to Paris, England, went to England, and let's see, went to Switzerland.
It was really like Jazz with the Philharmonic orchestra.
Yeah, only he had so many, he broke them up into groups. Then J.J. and let's see, who -- he went out with somebody else, Howard McGhee and those guys.
Yeah, He had sort of a pop unit then, / mainstream.

Yeah, mainstream. Then Thad played with Russell, a guy named Russell , who was a piano player, I forget his name. And -- oh, then we all met at the Salle Playal in Paris, Miles and all of us, and we all played together there. And that was my first trip to Europe.
Oh, it was late as that, '62?
I didn't realize that.
Yeah, 1962.
